name: NGC 7454 (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 7454, a slowly rotating early-type galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: ngc7454-hubble
story: NGC 7454 is a slow rotator, its stars moving without the regular rotation of a disk. Hubble's sharp view found no flattened core at its center, a hint that gas helped build it.

claims.text: NGC 7454 is one of the 12 slowly rotating early-type galaxies (ATLAS3D slow rotators) imaged by HST program GO-13324
NGC 7454 was targeted as a low angular momentum early-type galaxy

Hubble imaging showed the 12 newly imaged slow rotators, including NGC 7454, have core-less central light profiles, consistent with formation through accretion of counter-rotating gas or gas-rich mergers
NGC 7454 is classified as a non-regular rotator
